source.yle: Cambridge Pre A1 Starters, A1 Movers and A2 Flyers Wordlists 2025
source.preliminary: Cambridge B1 Preliminary Vocabulary List August 2025

words.definition: the skill or power to do something well
words.definitionVi: kỹ năng hoặc sức mạnh để làm điều gì đó tốt
words.hint: Listen for “ability” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “ability” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Her ability to learn languages helps her a lot at work.
He has a natural ability for solving difficult problems.
Speaking clearly is an important ability in job interviews.
They tested our ability to work carefully under pressure.
I admire her ability to stay calm during long meetings.
Online courses can improve your writing ability quite quickly.
Do you have the ability to finish this report today?
His musical ability developed after several years of practice.
Teamwork is an ability that employers often look for.
She used her ability to negotiate a much better deal.
words.imageCredit: Neda Andel ~SLooK4U Blog · CC BY-SA 2.0 · flickr · https://www.flickr.com/photos/31730451@N03/22130141674

words.definition: having the skill, time, or chance to do something
words.definitionVi: có kỹ năng, thời gian hoặc cơ hội để làm điều gì đó
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “able” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I am able to finish the report before Friday afternoon.
Are you able to join the online meeting this morning?
She was able to find a flat near the station.
He is able to speak both Spanish and French well.
We were able to book cheaper tickets online yesterday.
Will you be able to help me move house tomorrow?
They are able to work from home two days a week.
I feel more able to concentrate after a short break.
Only members are able to enter this private area.
She was not able to attend the conference last week.

words.definition: to have the skill, permission, or opportunity to do something
words.definitionVi: có kỹ năng, sự cho phép hoặc cơ hội để làm điều gì đó
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “be able to” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I hope to be able to travel abroad next year.
Will you be able to send the email before noon?
She might be able to help with your job application.
We should be able to arrive before lunchtime today.
He was not able to understand the long instructions.
You must be able to work well in a team.
They hope to be able to open a new shop.
I want to be able to speak more confidently soon.
Were you able to find a parking space nearby?
Students should be able to use online dictionaries in class.

words.definition: approximately; a little more or less than a number
words.definitionVi: khoảng; nhiều hơn hoặc ít hơn một con số một chút
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “about 500 students” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: There were about 500 students at the open day.
The journey takes about forty minutes by fast train.
It costs about twenty pounds for a return ticket.
We waited about ten minutes for the next bus.
She usually starts work at about nine o’clock.
The meeting room can hold about thirty people comfortably.
I read about fifty pages of the novel last night.
He earns about the same salary as his brother.
The film lasts about two hours and fifteen minutes.
We need about three days to finish the whole project.

words.definition: in a higher place than something else; higher on a page or list
words.definitionVi: ở một nơi cao hơn cái gì khác; cao hơn trên một trang hoặc danh sách
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “above” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Our flat is above a busy coffee shop on High Street.
Please write your full name clearly above the line.
The temperature stays above average for most of July.
Look at the large map above the reception desk.
Her final score was above the class average this term.
Do not put heavy bags above your head on trains.
The instructions above explain how to log in safely.
Planes flew above the city during the evening festival.
His office is on the floor above ours at work.
Keep the medicine above the reach of small children.

words.definition: in or to a foreign country
words.definitionVi: trong hoặc tới một đất nước nước ngoài
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “abroad” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: She plans to study abroad for one full semester.
My brother works abroad for an international company.
Have you ever travelled abroad alone for work?
They lived abroad for three years after university.
Sending heavy packages abroad can be quite expensive.
He found a better job abroad last summer.
We prefer to holiday abroad in the summer months.
News from abroad filled most of the evening bulletin.
Is it easy to open a bank account abroad?
She gained useful experience while working abroad last year.

words.definition: not in a place where you are expected to be
words.definitionVi: không ở nơi bạn mong đợi
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “absent” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Three students were absent from English class today.
Why was she absent from the important meeting yesterday?
He has been absent from work for a whole week.
Please email me if you will be absent tomorrow.
Her name was marked absent on the class register.
The manager was absent when the important client arrived.
I felt nervous speaking while the teacher was absent.
Several staff members were absent because of sudden illness.
You cannot pass the course if you are often absent.
Was anyone absent from the training session this morning?

words.definition: completely; used to emphasise a strong opinion or agreement
words.definitionVi: hoàn toàn; được sử dụng để nhấn mạnh một ý kiến ​​hoặc sự đồng ý mạnh mẽ
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “absolutely” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: The film was absolutely awful from start to finish.
I absolutely agree with your suggestion about the schedule.
She was absolutely sure about her final career decision.
That new restaurant is absolutely fantastic for a quiet dinner.
Are you absolutely certain this is the right address?
We absolutely need more time to finish this report.
His answer in the interview was absolutely correct.
I would absolutely recommend this course to adult learners.
The hotel by the river was absolutely perfect for us.
When they asked if I minded waiting, I said absolutely not.

words.definition: a way of pronouncing a language that shows where a person is from
words.definitionVi: giọng / cách phát âm cho thấy bạn đến từ đâu
words.hint: Listen for “accent” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “accent” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: She has a beautiful French accent when she speaks.
His strong accent made the speech harder to follow.
I love listening to different regional accents on the radio.
Do you notice my accent when I speak English?
The actor practised an American accent for the film role.
People often comment on my northern accent at work.
A soft accent can still be easy to understand.
She lost her accent after living abroad for many years.
Teachers should respect every student’s accent in the classroom.
Can you copy his accent in this short dialogue practice?

words.definition: to agree to take something offered, or to believe something is true
words.definitionVi: chấp nhận; đồng ý nhận hoặc tin là đúng
words.hint: Listen for “accept” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “accept” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I am happy to accept your invitation to dinner tonight.
Please accept my sincere apology for being late yesterday.
She refused to accept money from complete strangers outside.
The college will accept applications until Friday next week.
He cannot accept that he made a serious mistake.
Do you accept credit cards in this small shop?
They accepted our offer on the flat yesterday afternoon.
You should accept feedback and try to improve quickly.
We accept that the plan still needs more careful work.
Will they accept students from other countries next year?

words.definition: good enough; allowed or agreed by most people
words.definitionVi: đủ tốt; được hầu hết mọi người cho phép hoặc đồng ý
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “acceptable” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: This level of noise is not acceptable late at night.
Is casual dress acceptable in your office on Fridays?
Her excuse was not acceptable to the team manager.
We need an acceptable price that works for both sides.
Late homework is rarely acceptable without a clear reason.
The hotel offered an acceptable free upgrade to another room.
Is this solution acceptable to everyone in the meeting?
His behaviour was not acceptable during the client meeting.
Please choose an acceptable password for better account security.
They reached an acceptable compromise after a long discussion.

words.definition: the way or chance to enter a place or use something
words.definitionVi: cách thức hoặc cơ hội để vào một địa điểm hoặc sử dụng cái gì đó
words.hint: Listen for “access” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “access” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Students need a password for internet access in the library.
The building has easy access to the city centre.
Disabled access is available at the side entrance today.
I cannot access my email on this office computer.
Hotel guests have free access to the gym downstairs.
Do you have access to the shared project documents?
Public transport gives easy access to the airport terminals.
Only staff can access the private office area upstairs.
She lost access to her online account yesterday morning.
Good libraries give people access to useful information online.
words.imageCredit: Sarah Krichen WMFr · CC BY-SA 4.0 · wikimedia · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=94805312

words.definition: something bad that happens by chance, often causing damage or injury
words.definitionVi: điều gì đó xấu xảy ra tình cờ, thường gây ra thiệt hại hoặc thương tích
words.hint: Listen for “accident” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “accident” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: There was a serious accident on the busy motorway.
He had a cycling accident on the way to work.
Nobody was hurt in the car accident near town.
She missed the meeting because of a road accident.
Please report the accident to the police as soon as possible.
It was an accident, not something I carefully planned.
Traffic stopped after an accident near the old bridge.
I broke the glass by accident while washing up.
Witnesses described the accident carefully to the police officer.
They discussed road accidents during the safety training session.

words.definition: a place to stay or live, such as a hotel room or flat
words.definitionVi: một nơi để ở hoặc sinh sống, chẳng hạn như phòng khách sạn hoặc căn hộ
words.hint: Listen for “accommodation” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “accommodation” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: We need cheap accommodation near the university campus.
The travel agent booked our accommodation online last night.
Student accommodation in this city can be hard to find.
Is breakfast included with the hotel accommodation price?
They offer shared accommodation for young workers in town.
Our holiday accommodation was clean, quiet, and well located.
Please confirm your accommodation details before you arrive.
Temporary accommodation was provided after the serious flood.
Hotel accommodation in the centre is usually expensive.
She preferred private accommodation to staying in a hostel.
words.imageCredit: Queensland State Archives · CC PDM 1.0 · flickr · https://www.flickr.com/photos/60455048@N02/8279736902

words.definition: to go somewhere with someone; to happen or exist with something else
words.definitionVi: đi đâu đó với ai đó; xảy ra hoặc tồn tại với cái gì khác
words.hint: Notice how people use “accompany” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “accompany” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Can you accompany me to the interview tomorrow morning?
Young children must be accompanied by an adult inside.
She accompanied her parents on the trip abroad last year.
A guide will accompany the group around the museum.
Several symptoms may accompany this common winter illness.
He asked a friend to accompany him to the hospital.
Live piano music will accompany the singers tonight.
Would you like someone to accompany you home later?
Clear photos accompany the article on the company website.
Security staff accompany visitors into the main building.

words.definition: an arrangement with a bank or website to keep money or information
words.definitionVi: một thỏa thuận với ngân hàng hoặc trang web để giữ tiền hoặc thông tin
words.hint: Listen for “account” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “account” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I opened a bank account when I started my first job.
Please check your online account for the important message.
She forgot the password for her email account again.
There is not enough money in my current account.
You need an account to download the mobile app.
He paid the bill from his savings account yesterday.
Do not share your account details with strangers online.
I closed my old account at that bank last month.
Customer accounts are protected by strong passwords and checks.
Can I transfer money into your account later today?

words.definition: something bad that happens by chance, often causing damage or injury
words.definitionVi: điều gì đó xấu xảy ra tình cờ, thường gây ra thiệt hại hoặc thương tích
words.hint: Listen for “accident” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “accident” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: A traffic accident delayed our journey this morning badly.
She had an accident while cooking dinner at home.
The company investigated the workplace accident very carefully.
Call an ambulance if the accident looks serious.
It was a lucky escape after the road accident.
Drivers should slow down carefully to avoid accidents.
He damaged his phone by accident on the train.
News reports described the train accident in clear detail.
We discussed how to prevent accidents at work today.
Sorry — I deleted your file by accident earlier.

words.definition: a person whose job is to keep and check financial records
words.definitionVi: một người có công việc là lưu giữ và kiểm tra hồ sơ tài chính
words.hint: Listen for “accountant” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “accountant” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: My sister works as an accountant in a large firm.
We asked an accountant to check our tax forms carefully.
An accountant can help you plan your monthly budget.
He trained for years to become a qualified accountant.
The company’s accountant prepared the monthly financial report.
Do you need an accountant for your small business?
She spoke to an accountant before buying the flat.
Good accountants explain difficult numbers in simple language.
Our accountant found a mistake in the invoice yesterday.
Many accountants work long hours before important tax deadlines.

words.definition: correct and without mistakes
words.definitionVi: đúng và không có sai sót
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “accurate” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Please give an accurate description of the full problem.
The weather forecast was surprisingly accurate for today.
Is this information accurate and still up to date?
She keeps accurate records of every customer payment.
His summary of the long meeting was accurate.
We need accurate measurements for the new furniture.
The walking map is not accurate enough for hikers.
Machine translations are not always accurate for formal emails.
An accurate answer will get you full marks here.
Check that your personal details are accurate before sending.
words.imageCredit: Kheel Center, Cornell University Library · CC BY 2.0 · flickr · https://www.flickr.com/photos/38445726@N04/5279886008

words.definition: a continuous dull pain in part of the body
words.definitionVi: một cơn đau âm ỉ liên tục ở một phần cơ thể
words.hint: Listen for “ache” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “ache” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I have an ache in my back after sitting all day.
She felt a dull ache in her head during the meeting.
Hard exercise can cause muscle aches the next morning.
He felt an ache in his shoulder while swimming lengths.
This medicine should reduce the ache within an hour.
Do you get stomach aches when you feel stressed?
Cold weather made the ache in her knees much worse.
After the long flight I had an ache in my neck.
She ignored the ache until it became more serious.
A short walk helped ease the ache in my legs.

words.definition: to succeed in doing something after effort
words.definitionVi: thành công trong việc làm điều gì đó sau nỗ lực
words.hint: Notice how people use “achieve” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “achieve” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: She worked hard to achieve her main career goals.
We hope to achieve better results this school term.
He achieved a high score on the practice test.
What do you really want to achieve this year?
The team achieved success through careful planning and effort.
You can achieve a lot with regular daily study.
They achieved their sales target in June this year.
It takes patience and practice to achieve real progress.
Did you achieve everything on your to-do list today?
Students who practise daily often achieve more over time.

words.definition: something good that you succeed in doing through effort
words.definitionVi: điều gì đó tốt đẹp mà bạn thành công khi thực hiện nhờ nỗ lực
words.hint: Listen for “achievement” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “achievement” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Graduating from university was a major personal achievement for her.
Winning the contract was a great achievement for our team.
She talked about her achievements in the job interview.
Learning to drive felt like a personal achievement for him.
This award recognises his achievements in science and research.
Small achievements still help build your confidence over time.
Publishing her first article was an exciting achievement.
What is your greatest achievement so far in your career?
Team achievements depend on clear communication and trust.
Passing B1 Preliminary is a useful achievement for learners.

words.definition: from one side of something to the other
words.definitionVi: từ bên này sang bên kia của cái gì đó
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “across” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: We walked across the bridge to the old town centre.
There is a large supermarket across the busy road.
She swam across the lake during her summer holiday.
The news spread quickly across social media last night.
Please write your final answer across the whole page.
He looked across the room and smiled at her.
Buses run across the city every ten minutes today.
They travelled across Europe by train last summer.
A quick smile passed across her face for a moment.
Do not run across the busy street without looking.

words.definition: to perform a role in a play, film, or show
words.definitionVi: Thực hiện một vai trò trong một vở kịch, bộ phim hoặc chương trình
words.hint: Notice how people use “to act in a play” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “to act in a play” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: She wants to act in a play at college this term.
He acted the main character in the school drama show.
Have you ever acted on stage before in public?
They asked me to act in their short student film.
Good actors prepare carefully before they act each scene.
She acted brilliantly in last night’s theatre performance.
I prefer to act on stage rather than work backstage.
He hopes to act professionally after he finishes university.
Students act scenes from modern plays in drama class.
Can you act this short dialogue with a partner now?

words.definition: to behave in a particular way
words.definitionVi: cư xử theo một cách cụ thể
words.hint: Listen for “act” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “act” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Please stop acting like a child during important meetings.
He always acts politely with customers in the shop.
Please act responsibly when you are travelling abroad alone.
She acted strangely after hearing the unexpected news.
You should act quickly if there is a fire alarm.
They acted as if nothing unusual had happened.
Do not act surprised — you already knew the result.
He acted bravely in a very difficult situation at work.
Managers must act fairly with every employee in the company.
Why are you acting so nervous before the interview today?

words.definition: something that you do; the process of doing something
words.definitionVi: điều gì đó bạn làm; quá trình làm điều gì đó
words.hint: Listen for “action” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “action” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: We need real action now, not only more discussion.
Her quick action prevented a serious accident outside.
The company took action after several customer complaints.
Every action in the project plan has a clear deadline.
He prefers action films with plenty of exciting scenes.
Please explain the action you will take next week.
Climate action is discussed in many news reports today.
Their first action was to call for emergency help.
Good intentions mean very little without clear action.
The police action made the city streets feel safer.

words.definition: always busy doing things; taking part regularly
words.definitionVi: luôn bận rộn làm mọi việc; tham gia thường xuyên
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “active” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: She stays active by walking to work each weekday.
He is an active member of the local sports club.
Keeping active can improve your health in many ways.
Are you still active on that social media site?
An active lifestyle helps many people sleep much better.
She takes an active role in several local projects.
My grandparents remain active even in retirement years.
Students should be active learners during every class.
The volcano has not been active for many years.
He became more active after joining the local gym.

words.definition: something that you do for interest, work, or pleasure
words.definitionVi: điều gì đó mà bạn làm vì sở thích, công việc hoặc niềm vui
words.hint: Listen for “activity” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “activity” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Outdoor activities are popular with families at the weekend.
The course includes a group activity in each lesson.
What free-time activity do you enjoy most after work?
Online banking is a daily activity for many adults.
Volunteering is a useful activity for your job CV.
They planned team activities for the staff training day.
Physical activity can reduce stress after a long day.
Illegal activity online should be reported to the police.
Our club organises cultural activities every month for members.
Reading quietly is still my favourite free-time activity.

words.definition: a woman whose job is to act in plays, films, or television
words.definitionVi: một người phụ nữ có công việc là diễn kịch, phim ảnh hoặc truyền hình
words.hint: A job or role people do for work.
words.fact: Learners use “actress” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: The actress gave an impressive interview on national television.
She trained for years before becoming a successful actress.
My favourite actress stars in that new drama series.
An actress signed autographs outside the theatre after the show.
He married a well-known British actress last spring.
Young actresses often start in small local theatre plays.
The actress prepared her accent carefully for the film role.
Critics praised the actress for her natural stage performance.
Would you like to work as an actress one day?
The actress thanked her whole team in her short speech.

words.definition: the process of adding numbers; something extra that is added
words.definitionVi: quá trình cộng số; điều gì đó bổ sung được thêm vào
words.hint: Listen for “addition” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “addition” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Simple addition is easier when you practise every single day.
The new café is a welcome addition to our street.
In addition, we offer free Wi-Fi for all hotel guests.
Please check your addition carefully before you submit the form.
A small balcony was a useful addition to the flat.
In addition to English, she also studies Spanish at college.
The bill includes tax in addition to the meal price.
This software is a recent addition to our office tools.
Young children usually learn addition before they learn multiplication.
In addition, please bring a clear copy of your passport.

words.definition: the details of where a building is, used for post or finding a place
words.definitionVi: chi tiết về vị trí của tòa nhà, được sử dụng để đăng bài hoặc tìm địa điểm
words.hint: Listen for “in addition address” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “in addition address” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Please write your full home address clearly on the form.
I need the hotel address for the taxi driver now.
Has your home address changed at any time this year?
She saved the company address carefully in her phone.
Check that the email address is spelled correctly before sending.
We posted the documents to the wrong address by mistake.
Can you confirm your delivery address for me, please?
His new address is much closer to the train station.
Do not share your home address with strangers online.
The invitation includes the venue address and the start time.

words.definition: to respect someone or something and think they are very good
words.definitionVi: tôn trọng ai đó hoặc cái gì đó và nghĩ rằng họ rất tốt
words.hint: Notice how people use “admire” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “admire” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I admire people who stay calm under heavy pressure.
She admires her manager’s honest and clear communication.
Many students admire athletes for their strong daily discipline.
Do you admire anyone special in your close family?
He admires modern design more than old historic buildings.
We stopped for a moment to admire the hill view.
I admire your decision to learn another useful language.
Fans admire the singer’s voice and strong stage presence.
She has always admired creative problem-solving at work.
They admire colleagues who help others without being asked.

words.definition: permission to enter a place; the price charged to enter
words.definitionVi: phép vào một địa điểm; giá phải trả để vào
words.hint: Listen for “admission” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “admission” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Admission to the museum is free on Sunday mornings.
How much is admission to the evening concert tonight?
Student admission usually costs less than the full ticket price.
They refused him admission without a valid ID card.
Online booking includes admission for two adults and one child.
Free admission made the art exhibition very popular locally.
Admission charges are clearly listed on the official website.
She gained admission to a well-known university last year.
Keep your admission ticket until you leave the building.
Late admission is not allowed after the show has started.

words.definition: to agree that something is true, often unwillingly; to allow someone to enter
words.definitionVi: đồng ý rằng điều gì đó là đúng, thường là không sẵn lòng; cho phép ai đó vào
words.hint: Notice how people use “charges” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “charges” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: He had to admit that the whole plan had failed.
I admit I was completely wrong about the timetable.
She will not admit making that serious mistake at work.
Do you admit that you forgot the morning appointment?
The hospital will not admit visitors after nine o’clock.
He finally admitted the full truth to his parents.
Few people admit that they need extra help at work.
You must admit that the final results look impressive.
They admitted her to the course after a short interview.
I admit feeling nervous before important exams every time.

words.definition: a person who is fully grown; not a child
words.definitionVi: một người đã trưởng thành hoàn toàn; không phải là một đứa trẻ
words.hint: Listen for “adult” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “adult” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Only adults can buy tickets for this late-night film.
She started living alone as a young adult after college.
An adult must sign the form for anyone under eighteen.
Many adults return to study later in working life.
The museum offers cheaper tickets for adults on weekdays.
He behaves like a responsible adult in difficult situations.
Adult learners often prefer evening classes after full-time work.
Two adults and one child booked the hotel room.
Becoming an adult brings several new daily responsibilities.

words.fact: Learners use “amusing” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: The speaker told an amusing story about travel delays.
I found his comments more annoying than amusing.
That comedy series is amusing without being silly.
She has an amusing way of describing everyday problems.
Was the film amusing, or just a little boring?
His amusing emails make long workdays easier for the team.
The article included some amusing examples from history.
Children and adults both found the show amusing.
Try to keep your presentation clear and amusing.
I read an amusing blog post on the train this morning.

words.definition: very old; belonging to a period of history long ago
words.definitionVi: rất cũ; thuộc về một thời kỳ lịch sử cách đây rất lâu
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “ancient” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: We visited an ancient temple during our holiday.
Ancient cities often attract tourists and historians from abroad.
This book describes daily life in ancient Rome clearly.
The museum has a collection of ancient jewellery.
They discovered ancient tools near the river last summer.
I am interested in ancient languages and cultures.
The bridge looks ancient, but it is still safe.
She studied ancient history at university for three years.
Some ancient traditions are still celebrated today in this town.
Is that map of an ancient trade route?

words.definition: the joint that connects your foot to your leg
words.definitionVi: khớp nối bàn chân của bạn với chân của bạn
words.hint: Listen for “ankle” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “ankle” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I twisted my ankle while running to catch the bus.
The doctor checked her ankle after the fall.
He cannot play football because of a sore ankle.
She wore a thin gold chain around her ankle.
Rest your ankle and put ice on it tonight.
My ankle still hurts after yesterday's long hike in the hills.
The boot supports your ankle during long walks.
Did you break your ankle, or is it only swollen?
He crossed one ankle over the other while waiting.
Physiotherapy helped her ankle heal more quickly after the injury.

words.definition: a date when you remember or celebrate something from a previous year
words.definitionVi: ngày mà bạn nhớ hoặc ăn mừng điều gì đó từ năm trước
words.hint: Listen for “anniversary” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “anniversary” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: They celebrated their wedding anniversary at a restaurant.
Today is the tenth anniversary of the company.
We forgot our parents' anniversary last year and felt terrible.
The school held an event for its fiftieth anniversary.
What are you doing for your anniversary this year?
She bought flowers for their anniversary dinner at home.
The anniversary of the accident still makes him sad.
Our anniversary falls on the same day as the festival.
He wrote a short message for their anniversary.
Next month is the anniversary of when we first met.

words.definition: to tell people about something officially or publicly
words.definitionVi: nói với mọi người về điều gì đó một cách chính thức hoặc công khai
words.hint: Notice how people use “announce” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “announce” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: The manager will announce the new timetable tomorrow.
They announced that the concert had been cancelled.
Please announce your name before you begin speaking.
The government announced a change in the tax rules.
She announced her decision to leave the company.
When will they announce the exam results for this term?
He announced the winners at the end of the show.
The airline announced a delay of two hours.
We should announce the meeting time to everyone.
Did they announce who got the scholarship this year?

words.definition: a public or official statement giving people information
words.definitionVi: một tuyên bố công khai hoặc chính thức cung cấp thông tin cho mọi người
words.hint: Listen for “announcement” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “announcement” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: There was an important announcement on the station speakers.
Have you read the announcement on the noticeboard?
The announcement about the delay surprised everyone at the station.
She made a short announcement at the start of the meeting.
Please listen carefully to this announcement from the manager.
The company's announcement appeared on its website this morning.
His resignation announcement shocked his colleagues at the office.
I missed the announcement about the room change.
They published an announcement in the local newspaper.
Was there any announcement about extra buses tonight?

words.definition: to make someone a little angry or impatient
words.definitionVi: làm ai đó tức giận hoặc mất kiên nhẫn một chút
words.hint: Notice how people use “annoy” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “annoy” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Loud music can annoy people in the next flat.
Please do not annoy your colleagues during the meeting.
It annoys me when buses arrive late every day.
His constant questions began to annoy the teacher.
Does it annoy you if I open the window?
Spam emails annoy almost everyone at work every day.
She did not mean to annoy anyone with her comment.
Slow internet connections really annoy me during online meetings.
Try not to annoy customers with long waits.
What annoys you most about public transport in this city?

words.definition: a little angry or impatient because of something
words.definitionVi: một chút tức giận hoặc thiếu kiên nhẫn vì điều gì đó
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “annoyed” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I felt annoyed when the train was delayed again.
She looked annoyed after reading the long email.
Are you annoyed with me for being late?
Customers were annoyed about the poor service in the shop.
He gets annoyed if people interrupt him during calls.
We were annoyed that nobody had told us earlier.
My neighbour seemed annoyed by the noise from the party.
Do not get annoyed over such a small mistake.
She sounded annoyed on the phone this morning.
I am annoyed that my order still has not arrived.

words.definition: happening once every year
words.definitionVi: xảy ra mỗi năm một lần
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “annual” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: The company holds an annual meeting every March.
Our annual holiday usually lasts two weeks in August.
Have you paid your annual membership fee yet?
The school organises an annual sports day for all students.
Sales rose during the annual summer sale last year.
She writes an annual report for the manager.
Their annual income is enough for a comfortable life.
We look forward to the annual music festival.
Is this an annual event or a one-time show?
The museum offers an annual ticket for regular visitors.

words.definition: a machine that records phone messages when you cannot answer
words.definitionVi: một chiếc máy ghi lại tin nhắn điện thoại khi bạn không thể trả lời
words.hint: Listen for “answerphone” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “answerphone” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I left a message on her answerphone this morning.
Please check the answerphone when you get home.

The office answerphone says they are closed until Monday.
She still uses an answerphone instead of voicemail.
Did you hear the message on the answerphone?
I hate speaking to an answerphone after a long wait.
Turn on the answerphone before you leave the flat.
The answerphone recorded three calls while we were out.
He updated the answerphone message with new opening hours.

words.definition: a small insect that lives in large groups
words.definitionVi: một loài côn trùng nhỏ sống theo nhóm lớn
words.hint: Listen for “ant” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “ant” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: There were ants crawling across the kitchen floor.
An ant can carry food much heavier than its body.
We watched ants moving in a line towards the sugar.
Keep food covered so ants do not find it.
She studied ants for a short science project.
A picnic often attracts ants and other insects.
I saw a black ant on my desk this morning.
Ants work together carefully to build their nests underground.
Do not leave sweet drinks open or ants will come.
The documentary explained how ants communicate with each other.

words.definition: an old object that is valuable because of its age and quality
words.definitionVi: một đồ vật cũ có giá trị vì độ tuổi và chất lượng của nó
words.hint: Listen for “antique” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “antique” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: They bought an antique table at the weekend market.
This shop specialises in antique furniture and jewellery.
Is that vase an antique, or only a modern copy?
She collects antique watches from the nineteenth century.
The museum displayed antique tools from local farms.
Antique shops can be expensive, so compare prices.
He inherited several antique books from his grandfather.
We found an antique mirror in the second-hand shop.
Experts checked whether the painting was a real antique.
Do you prefer modern design or antique style?

words.definition: worried or nervous about something that may happen
words.definitionVi: lo lắng hoặc lo lắng về điều gì đó có thể xảy ra
words.hint: This adjective describes a person, place, or thing.
words.fact: Learners use “anxious” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I feel anxious before important exams at university.
She looked anxious while waiting for the results.
Many people feel anxious about job interviews these days.
He is anxious about flying for the first time.
Parents often feel anxious when teenagers travel alone.
Try not to get too anxious about small mistakes.
Are you anxious about tomorrow's presentation at work?
The long delay made passengers anxious and tired.
She sounded anxious on the phone last night.
Deep breathing can help when you feel anxious.

words.definition: any longer (usually in negative sentences or questions)
words.definitionVi: nữa (thường trong câu phủ định hoặc câu hỏi)
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “anymore” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I do not live in that city anymore.
She does not work here anymore after the company moved.
We do not use cash very often anymore.
He cannot run as fast as before anymore.
Do you still go to that café, or not anymore?
They are not friends anymore after the argument.
I do not watch that programme anymore on television.
The shop does not sell stamps anymore since last year.
Sorry, we do not take bookings by phone anymore.
Why do you not call me anymore after work?

words.definition: used to change the subject, or to say something is true despite another fact
words.definitionVi: được sử dụng để thay đổi chủ đề hoặc để nói điều gì đó là đúng mặc dù thực tế khác
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “anyway” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: It was raining, but we went for a walk anyway.
Anyway, let us talk about the travel plans.
I did not like the film, but my friends enjoyed it anyway.
The ticket was expensive; I bought it anyway.
Anyway, what time should we meet tomorrow after lunch?
He apologised, but she was still angry anyway.
I am busy, but I will help you anyway.
Anyway, thanks for calling this afternoon about the tickets.
She failed the first test but passed the course anyway.
We arrived late, but they let us in anyway.

words.definition: separated by distance or time; not together
words.definitionVi: cách nhau bởi khoảng cách hoặc thời gian; không cùng nhau
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “apart” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: The two towns are only five kilometres apart.
They lived apart for a year because of work.
Please keep these documents apart from the others.
His front teeth are slightly apart in old photographs.
We stood apart so everyone could see the screen.
The meetings are three weeks apart this term.
She took the machine apart to find the problem.
Friends can stay close even when they live apart.
The houses are built too close together, not far apart.
How far apart are the bus stops on this route?

words.definition: except for; not including
words.definitionVi: ngoại trừ ; không bao gồm
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “apart from” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: Apart from Monday, I am free every evening.
Everyone came to the party apart from Tom.
Apart from a short delay, the journey was fine.
I like all vegetables apart from cabbage and broccoli.
Apart from English, she also studies Spanish at college.
The room was empty apart from one chair.
Apart from the price, the hotel was perfect.
Nobody complained apart from one customer at the desk.
Apart from work, what do you do at weekends?
The film was excellent apart from the ending.

words.definition: a tall building that contains several flats or apartments
words.definitionVi: một tòa nhà cao tầng có chứa một số căn hộ hoặc căn hộ
words.hint: Listen for “apartment building” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “apartment building” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: They live in a large apartment building near the station.

Is there a lift in your apartment building?
The new apartment building will open next spring.
Noise travels easily in this old apartment building.
She moved into an apartment building closer to work.
Security cameras were installed in the apartment building.
How many floors does that apartment building have?
We met neighbours in the hall of the apartment building.

words.definition: to say that you are sorry for something you have done
words.definitionVi: Nói rằng bạn xin lỗi vì điều gì đó bạn đã làm
words.hint: Notice how people use “apologise” in real situations.
words.fact: Learners use “apologise” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: I want to apologise for being late this morning.

Did the company apologise for the delayed delivery?

I apologised for missing the meeting yesterday morning.
It is better to apologise early than to wait.
Why did nobody apologise after the problem with the order?

words.definition: words or a message saying that you are sorry
words.definitionVi: lời nói hoặc tin nhắn nói rằng bạn rất tiếc
words.hint: Listen for “apology” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “apology” in stories, messages, and everyday English.
sentences: She sent a written apology to the customer.

The company issued a public apology yesterday on its website.
A simple apology would have been enough for most people.

Did you receive an apology for the wrong order?
Her apology sounded honest and sincere to everyone present.

Please include an apology in your email to the client.

words.definition: to become visible or arrive; also to seem
words.definitionVi: xuất hiện; trở nên nhìn thấy được; cũng có nghĩa có vẻ

A message appeared on my phone during the meeting.

words.definition: the way a person or thing looks
words.definitionVi: cách một người hoặc vật trông
words.hint: Listen for “appearance” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “appearance” in stories, messages, and everyday English.

words.definition: a formal written request for a job, course, or official document
words.definitionVi: một yêu cầu bằng văn bản chính thức về một công việc, khóa học hoặc tài liệu chính thức

words.definition: to make a formal request for a job, course, or official document
words.definitionVi: Thực hiện một yêu cầu chính thức cho một công việc, khóa học, hoặc tài liệu chính thức
words.hint: Listen for “apply” in stories and conversations.

words.hint: Listen for “appointment” in stories and conversations.

words.definition: to come nearer to a person, place, or time

words.definition: to think that something is good or acceptable; to officially agree
words.definitionVi: nghĩ rằng điều gì đó là tốt hoặc có thể chấp nhận được; chính thức đồng ý

words.definitionVi: Về; gần với một con số hoặc số tiền nhưng không chính xác

words.definition: a person whose job is to design buildings
words.definitionVi: một người có công việc là thiết kế các tòa nhà
words.hint: Listen for “architect” in stories and conversations.

words.definition: the design and style of buildings; the work of designing them
words.definitionVi: thiết kế và phong cách của các tòa nhà; công việc thiết kế chúng
words.hint: Listen for “architecture” in stories and conversations.

words.definition: a part of a place, city, or country, or a subject you study or discuss
words.definitionVi: một phần của địa điểm, thành phố hoặc quốc gia hoặc chủ đề bạn nghiên cứu hoặc thảo luận
words.hint: Listen for “area” in stories and conversations.

They are building new flats in that area.

words.definition: to disagree with someone in words, often angrily; also to give reasons for an opinion
words.definitionVi: không đồng ý với ai về lời nói, thường là giận dữ; cũng để đưa ra lý do cho một ý kiến

Stop arguing and listen for a moment.

words.definition: an angry disagreement; also a reason you give to support an opinion
words.definitionVi: một sự bất đồng giận dữ; cũng là lý do bạn đưa ra để ủng hộ một ý kiến
words.hint: Listen for “argument” in stories and conversations.

Their argument lasted only a few minutes.
Can you explain your argument in one sentence?

words.definition: a large organised group of soldiers who fight on land for a country
words.definitionVi: một nhóm binh lính có tổ chức lớn chiến đấu trên bộ vì đất nước
words.hint: Listen for “army” in stories and conversations.
words.fact: Learners use “army” in stories, messages, and everyday English.

The film is about life in the army.

He left the army and started a new job.
The museum shows old army uniforms and maps.

words.definition: in different places nearby; surrounding something; approximately
words.definitionVi: ở những nơi khác nhau gần đó; xung quanh điều gì đó; khoảng
words.hint: This adverb adds detail about time, place, or manner.
words.fact: Learners use “around” in stories, messages, and everyday English.

words.definitionVi: lên kế hoạch hoặc tổ chức điều gì đó; cũng để sắp xếp mọi thứ theo thứ tự gọn gàng
words.hint: Notice how people use “arrange” in real situations.

words.definition: a period of two weeks

words.definition: used when something good happens by good luck
